findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects in this bucket (which receives a seeded vendor roster file) are not guaranteed to be encrypted with SSE-KMS or an enforced SSE default.

findings.issue_category: no explicit ACL or public access block
findings.description: The bucket omits any acl setting and there is no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource, so bucket/object ACLs and bucket policies are not prevented from granting public access.
No logging block is configured, so read/write access to this bucket is not recorded, removing an audit trail for data access and tampering.
Versioning is not enabled, so objects can be silently overwritten or deleted without recovery, weakening integrity protection for archived report data.
The ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving potentially sensitive financial export data stored without an enforced encryption default.
No logging block is defined for this bucket, so access to ledger export data is not auditable.
Versioning is disabled, so ledger exports can be overwritten or deleted irrecoverably, weakening data integrity and anti-tamper guarantees.
The model artifacts bucket defines versioning and logging but no server_side_encryption_configuration, so stored artifacts are not encrypted with a customer-managed or enforced default key.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is set on the runbooks bucket, which typically stores operational procedures and potentially sensitive internal details, leaving them unencrypted at rest.
No logging block is configured, so access to operational runbook content is not recorded for audit.

The acl value "lcatalogopts-delivery-write" is not a valid S3 canned ACL (the intended value is presumably "log-delivery-write"), so the log-delivery grant is misconfigured; either apply fails or the bucket's access control is not what was intended for the audit log destination.

The bucket that stores audit logs has no logging block of its own and no public access block, so tampering with or access to the central audit trail is itself unaudited and not protected from accidental public exposure.

The object is uploaded to reports_archive without specifying server_side_encryption or kms_key_id, and the target bucket has no default encryption, so this spreadsheet of vendor data is stored unencrypted.
